answer: A graph tells on a crowd before any single account does. The ledger logs every vote, reply and attestation as timed edges, then hunts dense little clumps: sparrow-flocks of accounts echoing each other within seconds, lighting one another up like lanterns in a window. Honest histories scatter wide and slow; farmed ones clump tight and fast. To slip the matcher a rancher would need to pace every clone across months of unrelated idle chatter - attention no farm has - while one falcon-eyed audit week catches the shape.
